# A02 audit and repair, 2026-09-15

**Later ruling applied:** `afe6690` resolved Q-CHAR-2 during independent review. The earlier
maximum-change marker implementation and synthetic recording test below are superseded by
the shared preview/downward-cap activation repair documented in
`2026-09-15-A02-independent-review.md`. Compatible current values are retained and capped to
new maxima; incompatible resource replacement is explicitly refused. Q-CHAR-2 is no longer open.
Q-CHAR-10/11 were also answered later and implemented in
`2026-09-15-A02-final-character-rulings.md`; their open status below is historical research context.

Research baseline: main `3b06832`; pinned Compendium
`fb83a789da8f0327a389c277a0c790b1648d5810`. This record begins before implementation.
Only local pinned Git blobs were consulted. Scope: delivered minimal Berserker/Mountain wizard,
R02 evaluator, R03 admission and sheet audiences; no broader class execution.

## Research and existing decisions

- `docs/character-wizard-spec.md#3-decision-system` and R01's recorded Q-R-100 answer already
  require Caelian to be visible, automatically known and excluded from paid language slots.
  Clean Heroes, **Caelian Empire**, says “All player characters know Caelian!”; **Culture
  Benefits** says “You know the language of your culture, in addition to knowing Caelian.”
  The original fixture's paid Caelian is obsolete. `chapter/making-a-hero.md`, **I Speak Their
  Language**, expressly allows leaving languages open. Replace that fixture slot with explicit
  `null`, retaining Vaslorian and the automatic grant; do not invent a replacement language.
- Q-R-102 in the same owning spec already chooses the two spoken-language tables, including
  regional languages, deduplicated. The clean Heroes **Languages by Ancestry Table** and
  **Vaslorian Human Languages Table** are the source pools; dead languages are excluded. Existing
  JSON restrictions to Anjali / Caelian / Vaslorian do not implement that settled decision.
- Q-R-101 already chooses any permutation of the selected source array, fixed class scores
  locked, new slots blank, and equivalent named/headless and drag-and-drop assignment.
  `class/fury.md`, **Basics**, fixes Might and Agility at 2 and lists arrays 2/−1/−1,
  1/1/−1, 1/0/0 “for your other characteristic scores”. Preserve the user-selected ordering
  interpretation; remove the old uncertainty label and fixture-only acceptance restriction.
- Q-R-103 is answered by `docs/research/fury-kit-eligibility.md` and the owning scope: ordinary
  kits follow the Kit grant, Stormwight kits the Beast Shape grant; playable v0.01 remains
  Berserker/Mountain only. No new policy question or Martial-only filter is appropriate.
- R02 `docs/character-derived-values.md` owns arithmetic and provenance. Local Fury **Basics**
  prints starting Stamina 21, Recoveries 10 and Might-based potencies; Mountain gives Stamina +9
  and stability +2; Recoveries gives floor(maximum/3). Thus fixture maximum 30, recoveries 10,
  recovery 10, winded 15, Might/Agility 2, potency 0/1/2. Retain R02's labeled Stamina-term
  interpretation and R03's first-admission Ferocity-zero interpretation; do not automate grants.
- R03 `docs/live-state-initialization.md` requires first admission from baseline and subsequent
  activation to retain live resources, recording changed maxima/resource names under Q-CHAR-2.
  That reconciliation question remains explicitly open in the owning character specification;
  a changed array has no maximum effect in the supported scope.
- Admission and build review are distinct from gameplay undo (`character-wizard-spec.md`,
  revision/review lifecycle and progression history; `table-spec.md`, history). Existing admission
  operations write records without gameplay journal entries. Root owns repair of the false-undo
  behavior; no arbitrary character/build rewind policy is introduced here.

## Findings, repairs and verification

Implementation and independent review evidence will follow below.

Additional pre-change source check: Q-CHAR-12 is already resolved in the current R02 specification
and question queue. `rule/character/potency.md` expressly says the potency characteristic is
“determined by your class”; `chapter/the-basics.md`, **Game of Exceptions**, makes a specific
exception prevail over a general rule. Remove stale uncertainty metadata, retaining Fury's
Might-based values and source provenance. No new ruling is requested.

### Implemented repairs

1. Paid Caelian is refused by the shared choice pool and displayed as an automatically known
   common tongue in both culture/career selectors. The 32 other distinct spoken languages are
   offered in both evaluator and UI; dead languages remain excluded. R01, R02 and hero fixture
   mirrors now explicitly defer the obsolete paid-Caelian slot. Ordinary repeated chosen languages
   retain the pre-existing warning behavior; this repair does not generalize the Caelian ruling.
2. All three printed Fury arrays and all nine distinct permutations are supported. New assignment
   slots stay blank, Might/Agility are locked, partial assignments are incomplete, overused/out-of-array
   values and attempts to change fixed scores are refused. `shared/evaluate/assignment.ts` owns
   transitions for dropdown, drag/drop (including moves) and named `characters.save.assignment`
   input. The latter is a real persisted, idempotent headless operation, not a separate calculator.
3. Removed resolved Q-R-100/101/102/103 and Q-CHAR-12 uncertainty labels from current artifacts,
   including the R03 hero projection. No formula, initiative policy or unique feature automation
   changed. Berserker/Mountain remains the supported class/kit subset.
4. Saved known decisions receive canonical pinned source/branch references. Duplicate decision ids
   cannot shadow one another through fabricated branch ids. Unknown decisions remain visible as
   invalid diagnostics rather than being silently discarded.
5. Review reads now search newest character history and query the Director's pending-status index
   before limiting results. A real pending review remains visible/approvable after 205 old decisions.
6. First attachment checks the destination campaign's paused/committed-combat party roster lock;
   an unattached character cannot bypass it merely because it has no prior combat-lock flag.
   Refused approval leaves the pending review, attachment and live record unchanged.
7. The sheet's stale A04 turn placeholder reads the existing shared encounter query. Its stale
   A05 Catch Breath placeholder invokes the registered `ability.use` operation, which owns combat
   allowance and FreePlay semantics. Integration of baseline-fed actions belongs to A05/root.

### Verification

- Focused source/evaluator/live-projection/admission/draft suites: **38 tests pass** (six files).
  The three R02 whole-result fixtures retain independent hand-computed expected values; arithmetic
  and all source quotes are checked against pinned Git blobs. Both printed language tables are
  independently parsed and matched exactly to the R01 pools.
- All nine distinct array permutations preserve fixed scores and fixture maximum 30. The full spoken
  pool, paid Caelian and every printed dead language exercise accepted/refused input paths.
- Persisted named and UI-transition assignments match after repeated values, partial selections and
  moving a score between characteristics. Retries create no extra revision; invalid assignments
  preserve stored revision and live state.
- Admission tests read persisted first-admission values, later live preservation, source snapshots,
  owner/Director/peer payloads, pending/stale/declined decisions, late roster-lock refusals and
  review histories exceeding the former query limits. A synthetic future baseline verifies all
  three `UnreconciledMaximumChange` records while leaving every live value unchanged; that is
  branch coverage of R03 recording, not approval of an unresolved resource-reconciliation policy.
- Focused ESLint passes. Whole-tree TypeScript was attempted during parallel work; current errors
  were outside this slice. Root owns the final coherent whole-tree check and deployment/codegen.
- `tests/browser/wizard.spec.ts` now exercises real dragging, locked fixed values, initially empty
  scores, automatic Caelian, a deduplicated regional language, explicit deferral and the new
  Catch Breath control. It captures wizard plus owner/Director/peer sheets and checks horizontal
  overflow. Root owns the final deployed browser run and visual inspection; not claimed done here.

### Remaining scope and question check

The latest owning specs and entire current character question queue were checked, including the
2026-09-15 source research. Q-CHAR-2 (played-resource reconciliation), Q-CHAR-10 (intentional
under-budget completion) and Q-CHAR-11 (skill replacement collisions) remain expressly unanswered.
The standard supported fixture avoids them. Existing labeled warnings/recording are preserved;
no user answer is inferred. Q-CHAR-3/4/5 and Q-R-201 concern later advancement, restoration,
reconfiguration or transfer workflows outside this delivered slice. Q-CHAR-6/7/8/9/13 concern
broader V1 options; printed v0.01 spoken-language scope and omitted Complication are already settled.
Q-CHAR-12 is source-resolved, and Q-A-200 is the now-actionable baseline integration dependency,
not a new product decision. No new question was added or old question reopened.

Independent code and rules review is still required on these repairs. This is the implementer and
researcher's evidence, not a self-approved verdict.
